title: Post-Processing Volumes 🎥
description: Apply colour grading, bloom, exposure, and depth of field to your scene.

slides.title: What is Post-Processing? 🖼️
slides.content:
# The Final Polish

Post‑processing applies screen‑space effects after the scene is rendered. Think of it like **Instagram filters** for your game.

Effects include:
* **Color Grading** – adjust contrast, saturation, tint
* **Bloom** – bright areas glow
* **Exposure** – simulate eye adaptation (auto‑brightness)
* **Depth of Field** – blur distant or near objects (cinematic focus)
* **Motion Blur** – blur fast movement
* **Vignette** – darken edges

Post‑processing is applied via **Post‑Process Volumes** – boxes you place that affect the camera when inside them.

quizData.question: Post‑process effects are applied to individual objects, not the whole screen.
quizData.explanation: Post‑process effects are screen‑space, applied to the final rendered image, not per object.

slides.title: Adding a Post-Process Volume 📦
slides.content:
## Step by Step

1. From Place Actors → Volumes, drag a **Post Process Volume** into the level.
2. Resize it to cover the area you want affected (or enable **Infinite Extent** in Details to affect entire level).
3. In the Details panel, scroll to the **Lens**, **Color Grading**, **Film** sections.
4. Check the checkbox next to any setting to enable it, then adjust the value.

Most settings have a **Weight** that blends between volumes. For a simple global effect, make one volume with Infinite Extent.

slides.title: Color Grading 🎨
slides.content:
## The Look

Under **Color Grading** (in Post Process settings), you can tweak:
* **Global** – Saturation, Contrast, Gamma
* **Shadows / Midtones / Highlights** – adjust colour tint and intensity for each tonal range.
* **White Balance** – Temp (warm/cool) and Tint (green/magenta).

Example: For a horror mood, desaturate, lower gamma, tint shadows blue. For a sunny field, increase saturation, warm highlights.

quizData.question: Which property adjusts the temperature (warm/cool) of the image?
quizData.explanation: White Balance Temperature shifts the image between blue (cool) and orange (warm).

slides.title: Bloom & Exposure 🌟
slides.content:
## Glow and Adapt

* **Bloom** – makes bright pixels bleed, creating a hazy glow. Control Intensity and Threshold (minimum brightness to bloom).
* **Exposure** – auto‑exposure (eye adaptation) adjusts brightness like a real eye when moving from dark to light. Disable if you want fixed brightness; use **Metering Mode** to control.

For stylized games, bloom is essential. For realistic, use subtle bloom and auto‑exposure.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Depth of Field for Focus

Enable **Depth of Field** in the Post Process Volume. Use a low F‑stop for blurry background, high for crisp. Great for cutscenes and close‑up shots.
